summary: Independently verified Phase 149O.20L.7O.2N.1's repair of Blocking finding B-149O.20L.7O.2N-1 (scripts/hatp_hardware_credential_admin.py::_cmd_enroll previously ran the real FIDO2 makeCredential ceremony before governance confirmation was checked). Verification only -- no production implementation change. Independently re-derived the fixed vulnerable checkpoint from git history (9e598106^ = cbcbcc0c, matching but not merely trusting 2N.1's claim) and re-derived the vulnerable event sequence directly from the frozen git blob (_run_enrollment_ceremony called unconditionally as _cmd_enroll's first statement, before --preview or confirmation are ever checked). Authored a fresh, independent 13-test suite (tests/test_phase_149o_20l_7o_2n_2_fido2_ordering_independent_verification.py) sharing no fixtures/assertions with 2N.1's own suite, proving: successful path event order is confirmation_checked -> provider_ceremony -> register_credential; declined confirmation yields zero provider/writer calls; --assume-yes is a pure prompt substitute at the identical ordering position (not an authority bypass -- the real security boundary remains OS filesystem write permission per HHCE-REQ-020, mirroring hatp_deployment_binding_admin.py's identical assume-yes precedent exactly); --preview never invokes the provider or the confirmation prompt and its printed description contains no fabricated credential_id/public_key; a forced 3-attempt persistence-write retry triggers exactly one provider ceremony and reuses the identical evidence object (NB-2L.4-1 retry semantics independently reconfirmed unchanged, not repaired); provider failure and user-presence timeout after confirmation both fail closed with no record created; no caller-supplied credential-identity argparse flag exists; no recover/import/restore subcommand or flag exists anywhere; revoke is non-regressed (not-found and declined-confirmation cases). Independently confirmed via git diff --stat (not trust) that hatp_principal_signer_admin.py, all 5 core writer/provider modules (hatp_hardware_credential_admin.py, hatp_fido2_provider.py, hatp_providers.py, hatp_piv_provider.py, hatp_hardware_credentials.py), and the HHCE-001 v1.1 contract text are all byte-identical between the vulnerable checkpoint and current HEAD -- only the intended thin-wrapper script changed. Independently recomputed the current implementation_scope_digest by calling the real production derive_implementation_scope_digest function directly: abfbffca527d3bf6d6ba610f6f5cd2d80bf113f9aa08f4339eb40322a8c077c4, differing from the deployed/certified 3b076a639b9f1b0c55facfd1a721d59d92a377d4bb63dce920843264e873a68e as expected (an already-bound frozen member's bytes changed); independently reconfirmed _frozen_canonical_paths() still returns exactly 38 paths with the script still a member -- no membership change, no HMIC-001 version bump required (no requirement text changed). Independently reconfirmed pyproject.toml's hatp-hardware optional extra already correctly declares fido2>=1.1,<2/cryptography>=42,<45 (packaging declared, unchanged by 2N.1) and separately confirmed the deployed hac-dell venv gap remains distinct and unaddressed by this phase. Performed an isolated git-worktree A/B regression comparison (fixed vulnerable checkpoint cbcbcc0c vs current HEAD, two full raw fast_green -n auto runs, no stash used as baseline): vulnerable 333 failed/8610 passed/4 skipped/9 errors; current HEAD 334 failed/8645 passed/4 skipped/9 errors. Node-ID-level diff isolated exactly 2 current-HEAD-only failures, both explained: the expected HMIC digest-mismatch consequence above, and one subprocess-timeout flake in an unrelated shell-gate audit test that passed cleanly on standalone rerun; and 1 vulnerable-only failure (a candidate-vs-origin/main currentness check, not attributable to this repair). Zero attributable regressions. No new Blocking finding opened by the --assume-yes authority analysis. B-149O.20L.7O.2N-1 -> INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED CLOSED at the FIDO2 enrollment pre-hardware governance authorization boundary (narrower than 'FIDO2 enrollment operational' -- real hardware remains unavailable, untouched by this phase). Overall verdict: A -- INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED, repaired hardware admin entrypoint ready for HMIC/deployment progression.
